steps: Side wall (J) 7.5"; wood trim no thicker than 3/4" at K1 8.5" and K2 7.5". Mantel 12" deep or less; a 12" mantel at least 20" above the top plate.
Insert bottom at least 5" above a combustible floor: Type 1 ember protection. Less than 5": Type 2, R-value of 1.4. Minimum hearth G 6", H 16".
Masonry fireplace to NFPA 211 only: no factory-built fireplace, mobile home or sleeping room. The chimney must exit the roof at least 3 feet and be 2 feet above any roof within 10 feet.

Masonry fireplace meeting NFPA 211, with a liner. Not a factory-built fireplace, not a mobile home, never a sleeping room. Don't connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance or to any air distribution or duct system.

For draft, the chimney exits the roof a minimum of 3 feet and at least 2 feet above any portion of the roof within 10 feet. Kuma's recommended flue heights run from 14 ft (no offsets) to 22 ft (90° offsets into an exterior chimney) — see the flue height card.

Pick a central spot in the main living area; an uninsulated basement or a garage is an inefficient location.
Have a certified chimney inspector clean and inspect the chimney and fireplace for code violations, cracks, damaged mortar joints or blockages. Re-line or rebuild if it's damaged or not to code.
Per the liner maker's instructions: a 6" flue liner meeting type HT (2100°) per UL 1777, not smaller than 6" or 28 square inches. Kuma recommends an insulated liner.
Uncrate; each piece comes in its own box with its own instructions. The insert is heavy, so lift it with a second person. Place it in the fireplace and level it.
Connect the liner to the insert, then install the fireplace surround. The surround kit includes the hardware for leveling the insert.
Install the catalyst and flame diffuser, then the door. Never run the insert without the baffle boards and ceramic insulation packaged with it.
Install the blower last. For the Alpine the parts list gives the KA-BL-03 variable speed blower with thermostat, 70 CFM.

panels.title: Smokes into the room
items: Bypass rod not pulled open (at start-up, or before the door was opened)
Cold chimney → reverse draft: open a door or window about 5 minutes, restart with small newspaper strips and kindling
Door opened too quickly → crack it, let the stove breathe a few seconds
Chimney or cap needs cleaning; screened caps can block in a few weeks

panels.title: Lazy burn / not hot enough
items: Chimney still cool → allow more time
Green wood or surface moisture → season about 1 year, cover the top of the stack
Shut down too soon → leave the air open longer
Catalyst plugged with ash, restricted chimney or cap, coal bed too small for the wood, or barometric episodes

panels.title: Won't shut down / short burns
items: Main door or glass gasket not sealing
Chimney too tall → check flue height recommendations
Fuel load too small or wood too large for the coal bed
Softer woods burn shorter than harder, denser woods

panels.title: Catalyst problems
items: Plugged with creosote: wet wood or bypass rod pushed in too soon → burn a hot fire, brush the face
Masked or plugged with soot / fly ash: bypass in too soon, or cardboard, coal or wrapping paper → brush or blow out the cells with dusting air
Lower efficiency: flames contacting the catalyst from excessive draft → less wood, lower air, or a damper
Poisoned by colored paper, cardboard, paneling, painted or treated wood

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Both controls are on the right: the bypass up top, the primary air control below. The bypass lets smoke skip the catalyst while you start or reload.

  1. Open the air. Slide the primary air control out, away from the insert, until it stops.
  2. Open the bypass. Pull it toward you (about ¾") and down. This heats the chimney quickly and keeps smoke out of the room while the door is open.
  3. Build the fire. Push ash and coals 2" back so the air inlet at the front stays clear. Build right on the fire brick, no grate. Larger split pieces go on the bottom, smaller ones above, kindling on top, then a fire starter such as shredded paper.
  4. Light it. You can leave the door slightly cracked to help it catch. Close it once the fire is well lit; never leave it unattended with the door open.
  5. Close the bypass after 15 minutes, or once the catalytic thermometer reaches its active range. Lift it and you'll feel it return to the closed position. Keep the air fully open for 20-30 minutes.
  6. Set the burn rate. Then slide the air control in. Turn it down too soon and the fire may go out or the catalyst may stop working.
Smoke puffing into the room? Check the bypass is open. A cold chimney can pull cold air down: open a door or window for about 5 minutes, then restart with small strips of newspaper and kindling.

burn.title: Air control and the catalytic thermometer
burn.html:
The primary air control (lower right) sets the burn rate. Slide it out for more heat and in for less; any point in between works.

Fully open · start-up or high2-3 hours
About 1/2" open · medium4-6 hours
Fully closed · low7-9 hours

Those are approximate burn times. After lighting, run it fully open for 20-30 minutes before you turn it down, but don't leave it on high too long or it can over-fire. The lowest setting is set at the factory and must not be altered.

The catalytic thermometer

It shows the temperature of the catalyst, the metal honeycomb that cleans up most of the leftover smoke. Keep it in the active range: anywhere in the light grey area is normal.

  • Above the range means you're past the catalyst's recommended 1300°F. Short spells are fine; slide the air in to cool it down.
  • Below the range means the fire is getting too cool to burn efficiently. Reload before the catalyst goes inactive.

The bypass

Closed is the normal run position. Open it only to start or reload.

reload.title: Adding more wood
reload.html:
1. Slide the primary air control fully open and pull the bypass open, just as when you light a fire. Wait 5 minutes so the coals wake up and smoke drafts up the chimney.
  2. Open the loading door slowly. Rake the coals, breaking up larger pieces, and push ash and coals 2" back to keep the front air inlet clear. Add wood and shut the door.
  3. Once the catalytic thermometer is in the active range and the new wood is well lit, close the bypass.
  4. Leave the air open until the fire is well established, then set your burn rate.
Note: the reload steps on p. 15 say to leave the air open for 10-20 minutes after reloading; the tips on the same page say 10-30 and 20-30 minutes, and p. 18 and p. 21 say 20 to 30 minutes.

Burn cleaner and longer

  • Only put large chunks on a very hot, active bed of coals. A small coal bed needs re-kindling first.
  • Small hot fires make less creosote than long, low, smoldering ones.
  • Now and then, look at the chimney from outside. If you see smoke, adjust the burn rate and the size of the load.
Smoke rolling out the door? Crack the door a little and let the fire breathe a few seconds before opening it all the way. If it keeps happening, the chimney or its cap may need cleaning.

firstfire.title: Your first fires
firstfire.html:
Start small: the paint is curing

For your first fire, start small and raise the heat slowly over 4 to 5 hours. The paint cures with heat, and while it does it gives off a smell and sometimes a visible haze. Keep the room well ventilated. The smell fades after a few hours of running.

Popping and creaking

Metal moves as it heats up and cools down. That popping or creaking is normal and will likely ease off after the first several weeks.

Lazy first fires

The first few fires often seem a bit lazy while moisture dries out of the brick. They get more active after that. A layer of ash in the bottom helps keep the coal bed hot, and a good thick coal bed with a full load of wood gives the best performance.

The surface color of the insert changes naturally as it's fired. The warranty treats that as normal.

wood.title: Choosing your wood
wood.html:
Moisture in the wood is the leading cause of creosote in the insert and chimney. Burn seasoned natural wood only.

Seasoning1 full year, protected from rain
Moisture content20% or less (use a moisture meter)
Recommended length16"

Air-dried, seasoned hardwoods generally burn cleaner and more efficiently than softwoods or green wood, and harder, denser woods burn longer. Keep your woodpile covered on top but open on the sides so air can keep drying it.

Never burn

Garbage, lawn clippings or yard waste, anything with rubber (tires included) or plastic, waste petroleum products, paints or paint thinners, asphalt products, anything with asbestos, construction or demolition debris, railroad ties, pressure-treated wood, manure or animal remains, salt-water driftwood or other materials previously saturated with salt water, unseasoned wood, paper products, cardboard, plywood or particleboard. Burning these may release toxic fumes or make the insert ineffective and cause smoke. Fire starters made from paper, cardboard, sawdust or wax are fine. Never burn flammable fluids such as gasoline, naphtha or engine oil.

Colored paper, cardboard, paneling and painted or treated wood can also poison the catalyst.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
The insert has an air wash that keeps the glass clean on its own: on high, the incoming air washes over the glass. If smoke deposits build up from slow burning, run the air on high for 20 to 30 minutes.

When you do clean it

  • Only when the glass is cool, never when it's hot.
  • Use a soft cloth and stove glass cleaner.
  • No steel wool, sandpaper or abrasive cleaners.
If the glass breaks, shut the primary air control and let the fire burn out. Don't leave the insert unattended, and don't use it again until the glass is replaced. Kuma replacement glass comes with its gasket already on.

Closing the door on a piece of wood that's too long will break the glass, and glass shattered by wood impact isn't covered by the warranty.

ash.title: Emptying the ashes
ash.html:
Empty the ashes when they get 3" to 4" deep. Leave 1" of ash in the bottom; it helps keep a hot charcoal bed.

  1. Make sure the fire is out. Never empty ashes with an active or full fire burning, because that will overheat the insert.
  2. Wear gloves. Ashes can stay hot.
  3. Scoop the ashes out through the loading door. The manual's ash-drawer steps are for freestanding models that have one.
  4. Put them in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid, and keep it away from the house.
Never put ashes in a plastic bucket, a paper bag or any other container that can burn, and never leave them near the house or garage.

Each time you light or reload, push ash and coals 2" back from the front so the air inlet there stays clear.

care.title: What to check, and when
care.html:
Chimney and connectorat least once every two months in the heating season
Catalyst (look only)at least three times a heating season
Door and glass gasketsat least once a year
Bricks and ceramic insulationannually
Note: p. 20 says the chimney and connector should be inspected at least once every two months during the heating season; p. 26 and p. 27 say every few months, with cleaning if necessary.

Chimney and creosote

Slow fires give off tar and vapors that condense in the chimney as creosote. Once lit, creosote burns extremely hot, and a chimney fire can damage the chimney and the insert. If it has built up, have it removed. Kuma recommends a licensed, professional chimney sweep.

Catalyst

Unhook the flame deflector by pulling it forward and look. If the catalyst isn't falling apart, crushed or badly warped, it's likely working.

Gaskets and bricks

Gaskets should feel somewhat soft; hard, frayed or missing spots leak air. Cracked bricks are fine if they stay in place, but crumbling ones need replacing.

safety.title: Safety around the insert
safety.html:
• It's hot while it runs. Keep children, clothing and furniture away. Contact can burn skin.
  • Don't over-fire. If any part of the insert or chimney glows, shut the air control off right away.
  • Keep the door closed while it burns. Crack it open only during start-up.
  • Never use gasoline, lighter fluid or similar liquids to start or freshen up a fire, and keep them well away from the insert.
  • Don't run it with broken glass, and don't slam the door or strike the glass.
  • Never use it without the baffle boards and ceramic insulation it came with.

In the house

Smoke detectors and carbon monoxide monitors are recommended in the same room as the insert; a stove that isn't drafting properly can let smoke and carbon monoxide into the home. Keep a type A:B:C fire extinguisher, checked regularly, where everyone knows to find it. The NFPA recommends one on each floor.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Kuma's limited warranty covers the original owner from the date of purchase, for stoves bought from an authorized Kuma dealer. It can't be transferred.

Bricks, gasket, ceramic insulation, paint3 years parts · no labor
Blowers, brick supports, removable wear items5 years parts · 3 years labor
Firebox, burn tubes, legs, glass (thermal breakage), door castingForever parts · 3 years labor

The catalyst

6-year structural: if a manufacturing defect makes it lose its structural integrity, Kuma replaces it at no charge. You return the old one, and it must not have been over-fired or used with unauthorized fuels. 12-year performance: one replacement at a 50% discount from MSRP, no return needed.

Register within 30 days at kumastoves.com or with the card in your owner's packet. For a claim, contact your dealer with your proof of purchase, the model name and the serial number.

Not covered

Surface color changes, glass shattered by wood impact, discolored plating or glass, firebox expansion noise, shipping costs, and damage from over-firing, the wrong fuel, accelerants, unauthorized repairs or improper installation.

specOutput.title: Output, efficiency & emissions
specOutput.html:
Heat output12,764 to 29,153 Btu/hr
Maker's website: Cordwood BTU's 63,000 (29,153 EPA est.).
Efficiency78% (High Heating Value)
Particulate emissions1.08 grams per hour
Average CO emissions0.45 grams per minute

Figures under specific test conditions. Catalytic-equipped wood heater meeting the 2020 U.S. EPA crib wood emission limits for wood heaters sold after May 15, 2020.

Emissions tested to ASTM E2515 and ASTM E2780 (report 0123WM013E); safety tested to UL 1482-2022 (report 0123WN011S); tested and listed by OMNI-Test Laboratories Inc.

The certification tag (p. 5) and the dimensional drawings (p. 6) are images only in the manual. Read the label data and dimensions from the PDF.

specFuel.title: Fuel & burn time
specFuel.html:
Recommended wood length16"
Moisture content20% or less
Seasoning1 full year
Low burn · air fully closed7-9 hours
Medium · about 1/2" open4-6 hours
Start-up or high · fully open2-3 hours
Maker's website: Burn Time 9 hours.

Natural wood only; burn times are approximate. The minimum low burn rate is manufacturer-set and must not be altered (federal regulations).

specChimney.title: Chimney & liner
specChimney.html:
FireplaceCode-approved masonry (e.g. NFPA 211)
Liner6" flue liner, type HT (2100°) per UL 1777
Minimum liner size6" diameter or 28 square inches
Roof exit3 feet min.; 2 feet above roof within 10 feet

Not for factory-built fireplaces or mobile homes. Any reduction in flue size may cause smoking or poor performance; Kuma recommends an insulated liner. Don't connect to a flue serving another appliance or to any air distribution or duct system.

specFlue.title: Flue height recommendations
specFlue.html:
No offsets in the chimney14 ft
30° or 45° offsets15 ft
90° offsets16 ft
90° offsets with 2-3 feet of horizontal run20 ft
90° offsets into exterior chimney22 ft

Too short a chimney reduces draft (back-puffing, creosote); too tall a chimney increases it and can keep the insert from shutting down.

specClear.title: Clearances & mantel
specClear.html:
All dimensions in inches. Side clearances are to the side wall of the insert; top clearances are to the top plate.

J · insert to side wall7.5"
K1 · insert to wood trim8.5"
K2 · insert to wood trim7.5"
Wood trim thicknessno thicker than 3/4"

Which trim edge K1 and K2 measure to is shown only in the clearance diagram on this page.

Mantel

Mantel 12" deep or less. A 12" mantel must be a minimum of 20" above the top plate of the insert. For a shallower mantel, the minimum height comes from a chart the manual shows only as a diagram on this page.

specHearth.title: Floor protection & hearth
specHearth.html:
Insert bottom at least 5" above combustible floorType 1 · ember protection only (no R-value)
Insert bottom less than 5" above floorType 2 · R-value of 1.4
Minimum hearth size G6"
Minimum hearth size H16"

Type 1 covers a raised hearth (min. 5" non-combustible) or a cantilevered insert (min. 5" air space); Type 2 an insert at floor level or less than 5" above it. Where G and H are measured is shown only in the diagram on this page.

specCat.title: Catalyst
specCat.html:
CombustorApplied Catalysts ACI-5M
Kuma part #KR-CT-01 (includes gasket KR-GK-01)
Recommended operating temp.1300°F
Functioning combustorin excess of 500°F, often above 1,000°F

Hybrid: secondary burn tubes re-burn smoke before it reaches the catalyst. Inspect visually at least three times a heating season; remove only if performance drops. Clean in place with a soft brush or ~20-30 psi air.

Replacement: pull the flame guard forward, pull the catalyst out by its 2 handles, clear old gasket from the cavity, slide the new one in with its tape and film on. Wrap any gap larger than 1/8" with extra gasket; it expands 2-3 times when heated.

Operating with the catalyst deactivated or removed is against federal regulations.

specParts.title: Service parts
specParts.html:
3 burn tubes · front / middle / rearKR-BT-180 / KR-BT-181 / KR-BT-182
Catalytic flame guardKR-FG-01
Ceramic baffle insulation setKR-IN-18
Door / ash pan gasketKR-GK-058 · 5/8" fiberglass, 8 feet
Glass gasket tapeKR-GK-034 · 3/4" fiberglass, 5 feet
Door glass (KA-DR-18-2 doors)KR-GL-18-2, includes gasket
Blower (optional)KA-BL-03 · variable speed with thermostat, 70 CFM
Maker's website: Blower Option: 71 CFM Variable speed, Thermostat Controlled.
The manual's baffle insulation steps (p. 22) say to remove the 3 burn tubes, then print "re-install the baffle and the 4 burn tubes"; the parts list on p. 25 shows three: front, middle and rear.

Burn tubes: unbolt with a 7/16" wrench, pull right, then down and out. Parts and support: your dealer, Kuma Stoves at 888-714-5294, or kumastoves.com.

review.notes: Image-only pages: p. 5 (certification tag) and p. 6 (dimensional drawings) have no text, so the guide gives no dimensions, weight or firebox volume; the catalog's dimensions, weight, firebox volume, minimum fireplace opening, flue collar note, cordwood BTU and heating area could not be checked against the manual. Checked and matching: heat output range, 78% HHV, 1.08 g/hr, 16 in wood length, 6 in flue, 7-9 hour low burn, side wall/trim/mantel and G/H hearth values, no mobile homes. 'Intake air requirements' heading on p. 9 has no text: outside air is not covered. Diagram-only: the mantel chart for mantels under 12 in and the K1/K2 trim positions (p. 7), and where G and H are measured (p. 8); values given as labeled, positions not transcribed. Ash: the manual's ash-drawer steps say 'if equipped on freestanding models'; the guide tells insert owners to scoop through the loading door. Confirm the Alpine has no ash drawer. The part at the face of the baffle is called flame deflector (p. 21), flame guard (p. 21, p. 25) and flame diffuser (p. 9). The troubleshooting draft-restriction example cites an 8 in chimney (p. 26, p. 27) and a 6 in chimney (p. 26); not used in the guide. p. 4 general warnings mention connector pipe and UL 103HT factory-built chimneys; the guide follows the insert-specific text (masonry fireplace with HT liner only, p. 9 and p. 11). No blower operating instructions in the manual (install order and part KA-BL-03 only). Catalog model number K-ALP-LE-1 does not appear in the manual (Model # K-181).
